position: Reform Conservation Programs (Reform NRCS wetlands and erodible land compliance and appeals)
proposal: The Mandate recommends removing NRCS authority to prescribe specific practices on a farm as a condition of eligibility for USDA programs, and instead requiring a general best-practices plan that a county Soil and Water Conservation District could approve. status_summary: No change to NRCS authority to prescribe farm practices, no shift to plans approved by Soil and Water Conservation Districts, and no Administration support for legislation moving compliance authority to states was found. S. 1495, the NRCS Wetland Compliance and Appeals Reform Act (introduced 2025-04-10), would raise the burden of proof on USDA, change wetland appeals and create state oversight committees whose members include active farmers, which matches the appeals part of the recommendation; no committee action was found. USDA's interim rule of 2026-07-29 treats wetland determinations issued since 1990-11-28 as certified when the producer was notified with appeal rights, which settles the status of older determinations but leaves appeal procedures and NRCS authority unchanged. In CTM Holdings v. USDA the Northern District of Iowa ruled for USDA on 2025-05-29, holding Swampbuster a valid spending-power condition, and the plaintiff later decided not to appeal according to an update reported by Iowa Public Radio.

timeline.event: S. 1495, the NRCS Wetland Compliance and Appeals Reform Act, was introduced by Sen. Rounds and referred to the Agriculture Committee; it addresses burden of proof, wetland appeals, state oversight committees and a ban on new permanent NRCS easements.

The Northern District of Iowa ruled for USDA in CTM Holdings v. USDA, holding the Swampbuster provisions a valid condition on federal benefits under the spending power and noting the plaintiff had not exhausted administrative remedies.
Iowa Public Radio updated its report to say the plaintiff in CTM Holdings had decided not to appeal, according to a Pacific Legal Foundation statement.

USDA published an interim rule, effective on publication, under which wetland determinations issued since 1990-11-28 are considered certified if the affected person was notified with appeal rights; comments were due 2026-09-28.
DTN reported that the interim rule was already in effect and that a national farm organization had raised concerns that the appeals process places the burden of proof on farmers.
